plan.chapterName: OpenStax Calculus, chapter 12: Vectors in Space
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional construction drawn in the first octant that locates a single point three different ways at once. The vertical axis is labeled z, the axis running to the right is labeled y, and the axis coming toward the viewer at the lower left is labeled x. A filled black dot at the upper right is tagged by two stacked lines of text, P(x, y, z) on top and P(rho, theta, phi) beneath it. A solid blue segment runs from the origin out to the dot and is labeled rho along its length. A small arc near the origin between the z-axis and that segment is labeled phi. Dashed orange lines complete the rest of the construction: a vertical drop from the point down to the xy-plane labeled z, and a segment from the origin across the xy-plane to the foot of that drop labeled r, with a small square where they meet marking the right angle. A second arc at the origin, between the x-axis and the segment r, is labeled theta. Superimposing all three descriptions on one point exposes theta and r as the quantities the systems share. The drawing introduces the ordered triple (rho, theta, phi), in which one distance and two angles fix a location in space.

elements: three coordinate axes meeting at the origin: positive z-axis vertical upward, positive y-axis extending to the right, positive x-axis extending diagonally down-left toward the viewer
arrowheads at the positive ends of the x, y, and z axes
axis labels x, y, and z placed at the arrowheads
single filled black point P in the first octant, above and to the right of the origin
two-line point label beside P: P(x, y, z) above P(rho, theta, phi)
solid blue radial segment from the origin to P labeled rho
orange dashed vertical segment from P straight down to the xy-plane labeled z
orange dashed ground-projection segment from the origin to the foot of the vertical drop labeled r
small right-angle square at the foot of the vertical drop where the vertical z segment meets the xy-plane projection
black angle arc at the origin between the positive z-axis and the radial segment OP labeled phi
black angle arc at the origin in the xy-plane between the positive x-axis and the ground-projection segment r labeled theta
foot point of P on the xy-plane at the bottom of the vertical dashed segment
coordinate readout panel showing the selected coordinate-system components
component highlight overlays that emphasize x, y, z, r, rho, theta, or phi depending on the selected readout

interactions.label: rho
interactions.teaches: The radial distance rho stretches or shrinks the point away from the origin while preserving the two direction angles

interactions.label: theta
interactions.teaches: Theta rotates the ground projection around the z-axis in the xy-plane, showing that this angle is shared by cylindrical and spherical coordinates

interactions.label: phi
interactions.teaches: Phi tilts the radial segment away from the positive z-axis, trading vertical height for horizontal ground distance

interactions.label: Coordinate readout
interactions.teaches: The same fixed point can be described by three coordinate systems; theta is shared by cylindrical and spherical coordinates, while r and rho measure different distances
Rotating the scene reveals that the orange r segment lies in the xy-plane, the orange z segment is vertical, and the blue rho segment reaches the actual 3D point

demo_steps.title: Spherical construction
demo_steps.narration: The point is fixed by one distance from the origin and two angles. The blue segment is rho, theta turns the ground projection in the xy-plane, and phi measures the tilt down from the positive z-axis.

demo_steps.title: Change the radius
demo_steps.narration: Increasing rho moves P farther along the same ray from the origin. The angles stay fixed, so the direction is unchanged while r and z both grow.

demo_steps.title: Rotate in the xy-plane
demo_steps.narration: Changing theta swings the dashed ground projection around the origin. The height z and total distance rho are unchanged, but the rectangular x and y components trade off.

demo_steps.title: Tilt away from the z-axis
demo_steps.narration: Increasing phi lowers the point relative to its radial distance and lengthens its projection r in the xy-plane. This shows why phi controls the balance between vertical and horizontal components.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a right-handed coordinate system with +Z vertical up, +Y initially appearing screen-right, and +X initially appearing diagonally down-left as in the source. World scale: axes should span about x=0..3.2, y=0..4.2, z=0..4.2, with the origin near the lower-left/center of the frame. Default point uses spherical coordinates rho=4, theta=60 degrees measured in the xy-plane from +X toward +Y, and phi=55 degrees measured down from +Z. Convert by x=rho*sin(phi)*cos(theta), y=rho*sin(phi)*sin(theta), z=rho*cos(phi), and r=rho*sin(phi). At the default this gives approximately x=1.64, y=2.84, z=2.29, r=3.28. The blue rho segment runs directly from origin to P. The orange dashed r segment runs from origin to (x,y,0). The orange dashed z segment runs from (x,y,0) vertically to P. Colors: axes and angle arcs black/dark gray #111111, radial segment blue #174f8a, construction lines orange-red #ff5a1f with dashed style, point black #000000, labels black with rho label in blue and r/z labels in orange. Keep all slider ranges in the first octant: theta and phi from 0 to 90 degrees so x,y,z remain nonnegative.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the axes as thin cylinders or line segments with cone arrowheads. Use CSS2D or sprite text labels that face the camera. Update P, the rho segment, dashed r and z segments, foot point, right-angle marker, and both angle arcs reactively when any slider changes. The phi arc should lie in the vertical plane containing the z-axis and OP; the theta arc should lie flat in the xy-plane. The readout toggle should not move the geometry; it should change the side-panel values and highlight the corresponding visible components.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for rho, theta, and phi: the learner adjusts each coordinate, the point P moves while the radial segment, ground projection, vertical height, and angle arcs update, showing how one distance and two angles determine a 3D location.

authoredContext:
In the spherical coordinate system, a point P in space (the figure) is represented by the ordered triple (ρ,θ,φ) where

In the Cartesian coordinate system, the location of a point in space is described using an ordered triple in which each coordinate represents a distance. In the cylindrical coordinate system, location of a point in space is described using two distances (randz) and an angle measure (θ). In the spherical coordinate system, we again use an ordered triple to describe the location of a point in space. In this case, the triple describes one distance and two angles. Spherical coordinates make it simple to describe a sphere, just as cylindrical coordinates make it easy to describe a cylinder. Grid lines for spherical coordinates are based on angle measures, like those for polar coordinates.

The relationship among spherical, rectangular, and cylindrical coordinates.

This figure is the first quadrant of the 3-dimensional coordinate system. It has a point labeled “(x, y, z) = (rho, theta, phi).” There is a line segment from the origin to the point. It is labeled “rho.” The angle between this line segment and the z-axis is phi. There is a line segment in the x y-plane from the origin to the shadow of the point. This segment is labeled “r.” The angle between the x-axis and r is theta.

By convention, the origin is represented as (0,0,0) in spherical coordinates.

discrepancies: The initial camera/projection makes the blue rho segment nearly horizontal, whereas in the source it rises clearly up and to the right from the origin to P.
The default yellow highlight overlays on rho, theta, and phi are extra visual elements not present in the textbook figure and partially change the intended blue/black styling.
The theta and phi angle arcs lack the small arrowheads shown in the source, making the angular measurements less faithful.
An extra orange dot marks the foot of the vertical projection, while the source only shows the dashed projection corner/right-angle construction.
The y-axis is angled more steeply downward than in the source, where it is closer to horizontal to the right.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is a recognizable and conceptually accurate spherical-coordinate construction with useful controls, but the default projection, extra highlights, and missing arc arrowheads reduce visual faithfulness.
action_items: Adjust the initial camera/view so the y-axis is closer to horizontal and the rho segment slopes upward like the source figure.
Remove or make optional the default yellow highlight overlays so the static appearance matches the textbook styling.
Add arrowheads to the theta and phi angle arcs.
Remove the extra orange foot point or make it much subtler to match the source construction.

feedback.rationale: The figure is conceptually accurate with high scores, and the remaining issues are minor visual fidelity refinements rather than plan-level or serious generation failures.
